content:
Dating reality shows have always been a popular genre, but Apple TV+ has never ventured into this space. Although its newly announced series "The Last Person on Earth" is positioned as a "docuseries" rather than a "reality show," it is still the streaming platform's first dating show.

"The Last Person on Earth" is hosted by renowned relationship therapist Esther Perel and described as an "innovative experiment."

Esther Perel is a famous relationship therapist and New York Times bestselling author who specializes in studying human relationships.

Perel is also the central figure in Apple TV+'s newly announced eight-episode dating docuseries "The Last Person on Earth."

The press release states: "On the show, seemingly mismatched pairs will be carefully matched by Perel and a group of matchmakers and therapists, then sent on journeys to some of the most romantic and remote destinations around the world."

It sounds very much like a reality show, but without the negative baggage that comes with the "reality" brand. I suspect Apple is trying to create a more "elevated" image for the dating show format, hence labeling it as a "docuseries."

The series has not yet announced a premiere date and is expected to debut in 2027.

Speaking of which, Apple also announced yesterday that it will adapt bestselling novelist Rebecca Yarros's latest romance novel into a TV series. It's obvious that the streaming platform is working hard to break out of its existing core genres of sci-fi, comedy, and thriller to venture into new territory.

Apple TV+ costs $12.99 per month, with discounts available through the Apple One bundle subscription.
